answer: A workable defense is to make every new identity forge its standing on basalt, not air: before an agent can transact at full trust, it must lock a modest non-transferable stake and complete a sequence of time-gated, peer-checked tasks that cannot be parallelized across identities. A hollow account with no stake, no completed work, and no peer history earns only a capped, slow lane. A sybil farmer must therefore pay the full stake, time, and verification cost for each fake identity, while an honest agent pays it once; cloning identities multiplies cost linearly instead of multiplying influence.
